name: Artspace Colorado Springs
headline: Artspace Colorado Springs is a 51-home, five-story, all-electric live/work building for artists and creative households at 60% AMI in the downtown Creative District, with ground-floor creative commercial space; Artspace Projects won a 2022 federal 4% award backed by El Paso County bonds, and the building was leasing in 2026.
why_it_matters: It shows how a small 4% deal closed with heavy non-housing money (a $5M state creative-industries grant, ARPA, foundations and a downtown development authority land buy) on a roughly $29.4M budget, about $577,000 per home (inferred).

status.label: Built and leasing (2026); 8609 not yet issued
status.detail: Artspace's January 2026 flyer listed rents and invited applications, its project page shows a March 2026 open house and now says 'Now Leasing!' with a move-in special. The deal is still on CHFA's 2026-09-21 active list, which leaves out developments with 8609s issued. No dated certificate of occupancy was found.

next_step: Watch for the deal on CHFA's 4% completed-developments (8609) list and for commercial-space lease-up.

key_numbers.meaning: One- and two-bedroom units marketed to artists and creative households, with an artist preference in leasing.
About $12.8M over 10 years; no state credit.

background.text: The project grew from a Colorado Springs Downtown Development Authority effort to give the Creative District a permanent home for artists; the DDA bought the site in 2019 with help from the GE Johnson and John and Margot Lane foundations.
In January 2022 Artspace and the DDA had about $18M of a then-estimated $26M budget lined up, and hoped to start construction in summer 2022.
Groundbreaking was held on 2023-04-07, with completion then expected toward the end of 2024.
El Paso County issued a $14.5M Series 2022 draw-down bond; bond counsel describes 51 units for low- and middle-income residents plus 20 commercial artist studios.

Artspace's commercial leasing flyer described the building as slated to open in spring 2026; the residential flyer dated 2026-01-06 shows photos of the finished building and interiors (inferred from the images).

discrepancies.text: CHFA lists the address as 345 East Costilla St, while Artspace and bond counsel give 315 E Costilla St.
CHFA lists $13,500,000 of El Paso County bonds, while bond counsel describes a $14,500,000 Series 2022 draw-down bond.
CHFA and Artspace's January 2026 flyer show 40 one-bedroom and 11 two-bedroom units, while Artspace's project page says 43 one-bedroom and 8 two-bedroom units.
Commercial space is given as about 1,775 sq ft on Artspace's page, about 7,000 sq ft in the 2022 news report, and 20 commercial artist studios by bond counsel.
Artspace's project page lists the one-bedroom rent at $1,171 ($1,266 gross less $95 utility allowance), while the January 2026 flyer gives $1,191 ($1,260 gross less $75).
